slides.title: My grandfather's watch stopped at 4:17. He never let anyone fix it.
For 50 years it sat on his wrist. Always 4:17.
Strangers would tell him: "Sir, your watch is wrong." He'd smile: "No. It's right."
When he passed, we found an old letter in his drawer.
1971. A railway station. A bomb. He had pulled 12 people off a burning coach.
The letter was from one of them. "You saved us at 4:17. We will never forget."
He never told anyone. He just kept the time.
lines: Some heroes don't want medals. Only memory.
